routeSelection.basis: The generic normalized target names no route. The current 2026–2027 guide identifies Klassieke Theologie as the main route, retaining the full biblical-language sequence and access to the university’s theological master directions. It represents the broad academic identity of the generic Theology bachelor more directly than the narrower Church and Society variant. This preserves the already reconstructed ordinary full-language curriculum; it does not select a route for UCR convenience.

comparator.name: Bachelor Theology
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–2027 study guide (p.10–11) explicitly names the main route Klassieke Theologie and its sustained biblical-language sequence. This general theological route is selected independently of UCR fit. The former 35-EC Religie en Samenleving Track 2 was converted from September 2026 into the 30-EC Theologie voor Kerk en Samenleving minor and a variant with language substitutions (p.76); that historical track is not carried forward. The official 2026–2027 full-time course overview fixes the 60/60/60-EC sequence. Its individual credited components are expanded here from the earlier year aggregates, preserving the same ordinary full-language curriculum and 180 EC. The third year retains genuine 30-EC internal/external minor space, seven continuing specialist/formation components and a 10-EC thesis. Missiology is one 7.5-EC module spanning periods C and D; formation entries repeated through the year are counted once. Current programme-page first-year examples are labelled 2025–2026, so the dated 2026–2027 guide and overview govern current formal details. The guide also confirms Christian Ecological Thinking and Theology for Church and Society as available minor directions; they inform UCR candidate concepts without being substituted into the comparator minor. exception.reason: UCR provides meaningful philosophical reflection on God, ethics and human agency, comparative myth, religious visual culture and analysis of civic life. Even strengthened with these contributions, the proposed programmes organise inquiry around general cultural meaning or secular public ethics rather than sustained Christian theological questions, biblical interpretation and religious practice. They therefore do not provide a defensible programme-level response to this Theology target.

candidateAssessment.concept: Christian theology, cultural traditions and interpretation
candidateAssessment.assessment: Tested the existing24course philosophical/literary/art/history composition and stronger religious-art/ancient-religion substitutions. Genuine God/Buddhist-self arguments, myth and religious artefacts support parts of the field. Their combined organising inquiry remains general culture and philosophy; no sustained study of Christian theological claims, sacred interpretation or lived religious practice follows. Not rejected by a language quota or degree-title test.

candidateAssessment.concept: Christian public ethics, church and ecological responsibility
candidateAssessment.assessment: Current Church/Society and ChristianEcologicalThinking directions independently corroborate these interests, but the strongest secular ethics/civic/environmental composition does not establish the Christian-theological reasoning and church-related inquiry central to those directions. Climate science, policy, public communication and community projects are real contributions, not documented Christian ecological theology. An unspecified project or minor cannot be presumed to supply that inquiry.

Community-engaged rhetoric, sociology, psychology and peacebuilding offer real practical and reflective contributions. They do not establish a sustained practical-theological programme addressing religious practice, worship, pastoral/diaconal work and their theological interpretation. Professional status alone is not the reason for rejection.

audience.programmeDescription: Theology at the Theological University Utrecht connects academic study of the Bible, Christian faith and religious traditions with questions in church, society and science. This curriculum follows the regular Classical Theology route, including biblical languages, systematic and practical theology, church history and theological research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related philosophical, ethical, literary, historical and cultural study, including material on religious thought and traditions. These contributions do not together form a sufficiently close programme in Christian theology, biblical interpretation and religious practice. We therefore show the Utrecht curriculum without proposing a UCR alternative.

curriculum.limitation: The curriculum includes 30 EC of approved minor space and a required 10-EC theological thesis. At least 10 minor EC must be advanced and at most 10 introductory. The thesis requires Methodology and 120 earned EC; an Old or New Testament thesis also requires 12.5 EC in the relevant biblical language. The ordinary first-year continuation threshold is 45 EC, with a plan to clear any remaining first-year work.
